summary.headline: Jindal Saw Q1 FY27 standalone PAT fell about 70% YoY to INR110 crores on MENA export shutdown, JJM delays and seamless API suspension.
summary.overview: Standalone total income rose about 13% YoY to INR3,756 crores, but EBITDA fell about 40% to INR341 crores and PAT fell about 70% to INR110 crores. Outward shipments to MENA have been suspended since March 2026 due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, and the seamless API licence was suspended from January to mid-June 2026. Management guided H1 to be softer, with H2 expected to improve, and said FY27 volumes should be flat with FY26. Abu Dhabi seamless (USD300 million, 3 lakh tons) and Saudi LSAW/HSAW JV projects are progressing, with commercial operations targeted for FY29.

segments.name: Standalone pipes (DI, LSAW/HSAW, seamless)
segments.commentary: Management reports pipes as a single segment and does not split volumes by product. Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in FY26 and is similar currently.

segments.name: Jindal Saw Abu Dhabi (subsidiary, DI pipes)
segments.commentary: Delivered about 34,000 MT in Q1 FY27 vs 48,000 MT in Q4 FY26, with sales restricted to in-range trucking customers. Order book is about USD188 million, or 1.77 lakh tons, giving 3-4 quarters of visibility.

segments.name: Jindal Hunting (51% JV with Hunting Energy Services)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR5 crores with a first-ever loss of INR5.3 crores in Q1, attributed to the API licence suspension.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volumes are expected to be broadly flat versus FY26, provided the current situation persists.
H1 FY27 is expected to be softer; management expects H2 to improve over H1, though it does not usually give forward numbers.
Middle East dispatches are expected to stay at about 10,000-12,000 tons per month, road-only, until the sea route reopens.
Seamless Nashik utilisation is expected to ramp from about September-October, reaching roughly 70,000-80,000 tons per quarter.
Abu Dhabi seamless plant (3 lakh tons, about USD300 million) targets commercial operation in FY29, with financial closure expected in the next few months.
Post-project term debt is estimated at about INR3,500 crores, excluding working capital, versus about INR500 crores of long-term debt now.
No domestic capacity additions are planned beyond the Middle East projects.
capex_capacity: Abu Dhabi seamless pipe plant: 3 lakh tons, about USD300 million. Long-lead equipment is being procured through LCs and cash advances, and leasehold land with existing civil infrastructure has been secured. Commissioning is expected in roughly 18-20 months, with 50-60% utilisation in year one.

Saudi JV (51% Jindal Saw, 49% Buhur): LSAW and HSAW mills of 300,000 MT per annum each. Land is secured and LCs are opened for selected equipment. Interim financial closure is expected within a few months, with execution in about 1.5 years.
Abu Dhabi DI pipe facility is 1 lakh tons. Management assumes about 50% utilisation across the new facilities, with peak utilisation in FY30-31.

Nashik seamless API licence was reinstated in mid-June 2026, and participation in API tenders has restarted. Utilisation is expected to dip for about a quarter before improving from September-October.
Capacity utilisation was about 60-65% in FY26 and is similar in the current period.
demand_pricing: Order book is about 1.78 million tons, of which about 0.75 million tons is export. Export order book is about 60% Middle East and 40% non-Middle East.
Export order split by product: about USD70 million LSAW, USD30 million seamless and USD40 million DI, excluding the 6.08 lakh ton Saudi helical SAW job-work order.
Exports to MENA have been suspended since March 2026. Management is exploring job-work options for the Saudi order and is engaging buyers on alternative routes.
Domestic JJM-linked water demand remains weak due to delayed central funds and title scrutiny. Some uptick was seen in state-driven projects and in DI volumes in Q1.
The company is diversifying exports to Europe (existing presence in Italy), Latin America, Southeast Asia and CIS. Historically the mix was about 30% export and 70% domestic.
Hydrogen-transport pipe qualification (API 5L 70,000 psi, Italy lab) is complete, but management has not yet seen significant ground-level demand.

qa_highlights.question: How should one view FY27 execution, and when will volumes recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Goyal said FY27 volumes are expected to match FY26 if the current situation holds. Middle East dispatches are fixed at about 10,000-12,000 tons per month by road until the sea route reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said interest is mainly on working capital and term loans, about INR70-75 crores per quarter. Q4 FY26 was hit by rupee depreciation, while Q1 was stable, and this run-rate is expected to continue if the rupee is stable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and utilisation for the MENA projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The LSAW/HSAW plants can be done in 18-24 months and the seamless plant in 18-20 months. Management assumes about 50% utilisation and peak utilisation in 2-3 years from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nashik seamless run-rate outlook after the API reinstatement?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation should dip for about a quarter and improve from September-October. Quarterly volumes are expected to be about 70,000-80,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure bottoming, and will H2 improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are under pressure from low utilisation and fixed-cost absorption. Management expects H2 to improve over H1, though Q2 may look similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What peak term debt is expected after the projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Term debt is about INR500-plus crores now and is estimated at about INR3,500 crores once the projects are complete. Working capital is additional.

risks_watch: The Strait of Hormuz blockade remains unresolved after the mid-June peace talks collapsed. Shipments to MENA are suspended and the Saudi job-work solution is still under discussion.
Pending JJM fund release and state title scrutiny continue to weigh on domestic DI demand.
Margin pressure is expected to persist into Q2 until utilisation recovers.
Working capital will rise as operations pick up.
The Delhi High Court order in the Jindal ITF vs NTPC matter is expected within about two months.
Seamless Nashik ramp-up depends on API orders following the licence reinstatement.
Watch whether MENA financial closure, the Abu Dhabi and Saudi projects and the peak-debt build-up stay on schedule.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term volumes and margins, with repeated acknowledgement of weak H1 and limited visibility. Confident on the medium-term MENA capacity build and H2 recovery, but evasive on product-wise volumes, marketing pipeline and hydrogen opportunity size.
key_quotes: Geopolitical situation between U.S. and Iran brought MENA region trade to a standstill this quarter by blocking the Strait of Hormuz.
So, in the first year, a couple of initial months will go for -- including in the longitudinal API grade, a couple of months goes for taking the approval.
Working capital is definitely directly related to the operations, because now operations are on a lower side, that's why the working capital is on a lower side.
